newsitem.title: USA: Hilton plans legal challenge to ITT plan.
newsitem.headline: Hilton plans legal challenge to ITT plan.

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp will mount a legal challenge to ITT Corp's plan to break into three companies, a Hilton spokesman said on Wednesday.

Earlier, ITT unveiled a defense against Hilton's five and one-half month-old, $6.5 billion bid for ITT calling for ITT to split into separate companies for its hotels and casinos, its telephone directories and its educational services.

Senior Vice President of Corporate Affairs Marc Grossman said for now Hilton's $55 per share bid will remain unchanged until Hilton, and financial markets, can put an accurate value on the three parts.
"We will absolutely pursue the legal options that are available to us," Grossman said. "It's real hard to say what the next steps are until we have more information."
He said Hilton's management would wait and see how the market valued ITT's plan before changing its $55 per share bid. "We have no plans to do that," Grossman said.
He also said any decision to revise its bid to target only the company holding ITT's hotels and casinos, to be called ITT Destinations Inc, would again depend on market valuations.
ITT gained 4-3/4 to 67-3/8 by late afternoon, but Grossman said one day is not a good indicator of long-term value.

He declined to provide timing for Hilton's decision-making process. Hilton is scheduled to release its second quarter earnings on July 22 and he said it is unlikely the company will announce a full strategy at that time.
Hilton shares gained 6/16 to settle at 29-9/16.

Legally, Hilton likely will amend its current lawsuit against ITT in U.S. District Court in Las Vegas, Nevada. Grossman said it is too soon to say exactly which provisions of ITT's plan, which includes a staggering of the terms for some board members, Hilton would attack.
